text:
li: Heads up — after the fused-attn kernel rollout in prod-us-efa last night we're seeing a 12-20% tail latency regression on 8x A100 jobs. Baseline before rollout was ~120ms p95, now ~140-145ms.

maya: ugh. which path is regressing? generation latency, kv-cache hits, or batched throughput?

li: generation p50 mostly stable, p95/p99 worse. profiler points to lots of tiny all-reduce ops between micro-batches. looks like the kernel split increased frequency of small comms. KV-cache miss rate is slightly up (~2%), but that's not enough to explain the tail.

samir: can you paste the nvprof/nsys snippet?

li: sure, here are the key slices from nsys (trimmed):
```
# nsys summary (sample)
Timeline: rank0
compute_kernels:  42%
allreduce_calls:   38% (many small calls, avg 60us)
cudaMemcpy:       10%
stall_due_to_sync:  8%

callstack top: fused_attn_forward -> split_qkv -> attn_kern_v2 -> post_attn_allreduce
```

li: NCCL traces show ~1.4k allreduce calls per batch vs ~400 before. message size distribution shifted toward many 1-8KB messages.

oren: that rings bell — fused-attn changed chunking to optimize kernel reuse, but it fragmented tensor segments across TP shards. small messages kill EFA (host-network) because latency dominates. NVLink intra-node was ok, but cross-node EFA is expensive for high-call-rate patterns.

maya: right — NVLink-connected boards mask small-message overhead; EFA/IB amplify it. Do we have host vs device split numbers?

li: yep: when the pipeline runs fully intra-node (NVLink), allreduce time % drops 20% relative to cross-node EFA. I attached the micro-latency histogram: cross-node median allreduce 70us -> 220us for small msgs.

samir: KV cache behavior — could repeated small fetches be causing cross-GPU KV pull chatter? If fused kernel changed KV packing, we might be querying shards more often.

li: we saw a slight increase in cross-GPU KV fetches due to different prefix handling in the new kernel. It's additive but the main multiplier is the all-reduce fragmentation.

oren: plan suggestion: two-pronged: 1) add topology-aware aggregation to grouping layer so we coalesce small tensors per iteration into fewer allreduce calls (prefer intra-node aggregation first). 2) adjust batching heuristic: increase micro-batch aggregation threshold when running on EFA-hosted instances.

maya: +1. also we should consider toggling the fused-attn kernel canary for EFA regions until we have coalescing. Quick rollback for hosted region if rollout is global.

devops-bot: deploy pipeline: rolling canary https://ci/1234 started by maya — will target prod-us-efa subset.

samir: implementation detail: grouping can be a small scheduler layer — collect per-step small tensors, sort by destination (intra-node first), pack into a single buffer, do one allreduce, then unpack. Need to ensure we don't increase device memory pressure.

li: I prototyped a packing approach — results on a 2-node test: single allreduce for packed tensors reduced allreduce time from 220us -> 95us for the same payload, and end-to-end p95 dropped ~18% on that test. Code snippet:
```python
# pseudo: pack small tensors before allreduce
buffers = []
for t in small_tensors:
  buffers.append(t.view(-1))
packed = torch.cat(buffers)
nccl.all_reduce(packed)
# then split back
```

oren: nice. also check NCCL_COLLNET and tree algorithms config — for EFA tree/ring choice matters. Can we flip NCCL_ALGO to 'tree' for medium msg sizes?

li: we tested NCCL_ALGO=ring vs tree. ring wins for large contiguous buffers; tree helps slightly when there are many small collective ops, but packing is still the big win.

maya: ops: (1) land packing + topology-aware prefer intra-node packing (PR in review), (2) add heuristic to increase micro-batch pack threshold on EFA (runtime config), (3) run canary rollback plan if regression persists. Who wants to own the canary gating?

oren: I'll own gating and the infra checks (topo detection, per-region metric monitor). I'll add a per-region SLO alert that auto-pauses rollout if p95 delta > 8% for 30m.

samir: I'll finish the packing PR and add unit tests for correct unpacking and mem overhead guard. Also adding a perf test (8xA100 EFA) to perf-suite.

li: I'll run extended profiling across PCIe-only hosts vs NVLink vs EFA to produce a short doc mapping message-size -> recommended pack thresholds. Will post results here tomorrow.

infra-bot: perf-suite job #987 queued (8xA100-efa) — ETA 2h.

maya: thanks all. prioritize shipping packing + heuristic. If packing reduces cross-node allreduce calls we should recover most of the tail. After that we can iterate on kernel chunking to avoid fragmenting in the first place. :thumbsup:

li: one more note — we should also expose a runtime flag to force 'monolithic' attention chunks for customers on dedicated infra that prefer lower latency over memory. Might be a quick short-term opt-out.

maya: agreed. create a small RFC for the runtime flag and include docs for when to use it.

li: will do.

samir: cool. I'll merge the PR behind a feature flag so we can A/B test.

maya: awesome. thanks team — update in this thread after the canary results. :eyes:
